scope: Selected battles with clear infobox outcomes. Belligerents and named commanders/leaders follow the linked Wikipedia infoboxes; context appears after each round.

battles.name: Battle of Marathon
battles.note: The exact modern-calendar date is debated; 12 September is the date used in the cited infobox.

battles.name: Battle of Thermopylae
battles.note: The Persians won the battle. The infobox gives competing dates between July and September 480 BC.

battles.name: Battle of Gaugamela
battles.note: Also called the Battle of Arbela.

battles.name: Battle of Cannae
battles.note: The Hasdrubal listed here is Hannibal’s cavalry officer, not his brother Hasdrubal Barca.

battles.name: Battle of Zama
battles.note: The current battle infobox names only these two commanders; the wider narrative includes subordinate commanders.

battles.name: Battle of Bouvines
battles.note: Includes the infobox’s expanded commander lists; Ferrand appears twice there but is counted once. “Philip II” means the French king; the opposing Philip of Namur requires his territorial name.

battles.name: Battle of Ain Jalut
battles.note: Al-Ashraf Musa is listed on the Mongol side in the battle infobox, but withdrew his forces under a secret agreement with Qutuz.

sources.title: Wikipedia — Al-Ashraf Musa, Emir of Homs

battles.name: Battle of Bannockburn

commanders.name: Humphrey de Bohun, Earl of Hereford
Aymer de Valence, Earl of Pembroke
Gilbert de Clare, Earl of Gloucester

battles.note: Alexander Seton defected from the English army between the two days of fighting; the infobox lists him on the Scottish side.

commanders.name: William de Bohun, Earl of Northampton

battles.name: Battle of Poitiers
battles.note: This is the 1356 battle, not the 732 battle also known as Tours. The current infobox names one commander per side.

commanders.name: Michael de la Pole, 3rd Earl of Suffolk

battles.name: Battle of Grunwald
battles.note: Also known as the First Battle of Tannenberg and the Battle of Žalgiris; this is the 1410 battle, not Tannenberg in 1914.

battles.name: Fall of Constantinople
battles.note: The siege ended with the Ottoman capture of the city. The defending coalition includes foreign contingents and volunteers, rather than full national armies; the roster follows the infobox, including the traditionally reported Ulubatlı Hasan.

battles.name: Battle of Cajamarca
battles.note: Also described as the Cajamarca massacre: Spanish troops ambushed the Inca ruler and his largely unarmed entourage. Atahualpa was captured; the conquest of the empire was not completed that day.

battles.name: First Battle of Panipat
battles.note: Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodi, who died in the battle. The victory established the basis for Mughal rule in northern India.

battles.name: Battle of Mohács
battles.note: King Louis II died during the defeat. Hungary’s later division between rival powers was a consequence of the crisis, rather than an immediate partition completed on the battlefield.

battles.name: Battle of Lepanto
battles.note: This was a naval victory for the Holy League. It did not reverse the Ottoman conquest of Cyprus.

battles.name: Battle of Nagashino
battles.note: The infobox roster covers the siege and associated field battle. Some listed leaders had wider campaign roles. Claims about systematic three-rank volley fire are debated.

battles.name: Battle of Breitenfeld
battles.note: The Swedish army won despite the early rout of its Saxon allies. This is the 1631 battle, not the second battle at Breitenfeld in 1642.

battles.name: Battle of Naseby
battles.note: The Parliamentarian New Model Army destroyed the main Royalist field army; the First English Civil War continued into 1646.

battles.name: Siege and Battle of Vienna
battles.note: The siege lasted from July; the relief battle on September 12 ended it. Starhemberg commanded the city garrison, while the other coalition leaders commanded the relief army.

sources.title: Wikipedia — Siege and Battle of Vienna

battles.name: Battle of Blenheim
battles.note: The Grand Alliance won and captured Tallard. The date is Gregorian; contemporary English accounts may use August 2, Old Style.

battles.name: Battle of Poltava
battles.note: Cossack forces were divided between the two coalitions. Charles XII was wounded before the battle, and Rehnskiöld directed the Swedish army. July 8 is Gregorian; June 27 is the Julian date.

battles.name: Battle of Culloden
battles.note: The government victory ended the Jacobite rising of 1745. This was a dynastic civil conflict, not a simple England-versus-Scotland battle.

battles.name: Battle of Plassey
battles.note: The infobox places Mir Jafar and the conspirators on the victorious side. Its roster includes political and financial supporters as well as field commanders; several Bengali contingents withheld support from the nawab.

battles.name: Battle of the Plains of Abraham

commanders.name: Louis Du Pont Duchambon de Vergor

battles.note: Also called the Battle of Quebec. Wolfe and Montcalm were mortally wounded. The infobox includes leaders involved in the wider siege and defence, not only officers present in the brief main engagement.

sources.title: Wikipedia — Battle of the Plains of Abraham

battles.name: Siege of Yorktown
battles.note: The roster covers the siege, Gloucester operations and supporting fleet. The Franco-American victory led to Cornwallis’s surrender but did not formally end the war until the 1783 peace.

battles.name: Battle of Austerlitz
battles.note: The French-led army defeated the Russian–Austrian coalition.

battles.name: Battle of Trafalgar
battles.note: Nelson was killed during the British victory.

battles.name: Battle of Waterloo
battles.note: Wellington's multinational army and Blücher's Prussians defeated Napoleon.

battles.name: Battle of New Orleans
battles.note: Fought after the Treaty of Ghent was signed, but before ratification and news of peace reached the armies.

battles.name: Battle of San Jacinto
battles.note: Santa Anna was captured the following day; the victory secured Texian control.

battles.name: Battle of Gettysburg
battles.note: The Union victory halted Lee's invasion of the North.

battles.name: Battle of Sedan
battles.note: Napoleon III and the Army of Châlons were captured; the war continued under a new French government.

battles.name: Battle of Adwa
battles.note: Italy subsequently recognized Ethiopian sovereignty.

battles.name: Battle of Omdurman
battles.note: The Anglo-Egyptian victory was followed by the defeat of the remaining Mahdist forces in 1899.

battles.name: Battle of Tsushima
battles.note: Japan destroyed or captured most of the Russian fleet.

battles.name: Battle of Tannenberg
battles.note: The encirclement destroyed most of Russia's Second Army.

battles.name: Battle of Midway
battles.note: Four Japanese fleet carriers were lost.

battles.name: Battle of Stalingrad
battles.note: The infobox includes political leaders, high command and commanders across the wider Stalingrad campaign.

battles.name: Battle of Dien Bien Phu
battles.note: The infobox also lists American transport support and Chinese support; the opposing ground forces were French Union and Viet Minh.

sources.title: Battle of Dien Bien Phu — Wikipedia

battles.name: Naval Battle of Guadalcanal
battles.note: The overall four-day engagement was an American victory despite heavy losses and varying outcomes in individual night actions.
